name: Nordkette
kurzbeschreibung: Innsbruck’s Hausberg – reach the summit at 2,256 m in just 20 minutes from the city center via the Hungerburgbahn.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Nordkette reigns as the indisputable icon of Innsbruck, reverently crowned the "Jewel of the Alps." Nowhere else on Earth does high-alpine wilderness meet urban cosmopolitan vibrancy so dramatically: aboard the futuristic Nordkettenbahnen funicular and cable cars, travelers ascend from the gothic Golden Roof in the city center directly into the sheer limestone arena of the Karwendel Nature Park at 2,256 meters in less than 20 minutes. The journey itself is an architectural masterpiece, featuring shell-like stations conceived by legendary architect Zaha Hadid. Arriving at the Seegrube plateau (1,905 m) and the panoramic Hafelekar summit station ("Top of Innsbruck"), visitors encounter a breathtaking dichotomy: looking south, Innsbruck glitters deep in the Inn Valley backed by glaciated Stubai peaks; turning north, an endless labyrinth of wild Karwendel limestone towers stretches toward the horizon.

Route & Requirements

Recreational pursuits range from casual panoramic strolls to extreme alpine mountaineering. The essential family classic is the short ascent from Hafelekar terminal to the Hafelekarspitze summit cross (2,334 m): an engineered path reaches the peak in 15 to 20 minutes (easy grade T1, sturdy walking shoes required). For technical mountaineers, the iconic Innsbruck Via Ferrata begins at the ridge, traversing seven sheer limestone needles and exposed pinnacles across two demanding stages (rated grade C/D; certified climbing set, helmet, and steel nerves mandatory). One of Tyrol's most celebrated high-altitude trails is the Goetheweg: setting out from Hafelekar, it hugs precipitous crags above the valley before traversing into the untouched alpine sanctuary of the Pfeishütte refuge (4.5 to 5 hours round trip, moderate grade T2). In winter, elite freeriders tackle the Karrinne—with a 70% pitch, it is one of Europe's steepest marked ski descents. Sturdy boots and windproof layers are vital, as mountain breezes chill quickly. Dogs riding cable cars require leashes and muzzles.

Visit & Arrival

The lower funicular terminal sits directly in central Innsbruck at Congress station (Rennweg), a short 5-minute stroll from the Golden Roof. City buses and tram lines stop directly at the entrance. Motorists can park in the underground Congress Garage (discounted parking validated with mountain lift ticket purchase). Cable cars operate daily between 8:30 AM and 5:30 PM departures every 15 minutes.

Tips

Disembark at the Hungerburg midpoint to explore the Alpenzoo Innsbruck, the highest-altitude zoo in Europe showcasing native bears, lynx, and alpine ibex. Late in the day, unwind on the panoramic deck of the Seegrube Restaurant with Tyrolean dumplings as the setting sun ignites the limestone ramparts in magnificent pink Alpenglow.
preis: Top of Innsbruck Bergbahnticket ca. 44 € (Hin- und Rückfahrt)
